name: Taronga Field Conservation Grants
summary: Biennial grants for on-ground conservation projects around the world, open to NGOs, community groups and individuals. The 2026 round has closed; the funded period of that round runs January 2027 to December 2028.

eligibility.rule: Project delivers clear, measurable benefits for species or habitats
Project aligns with relevant Sustainable Development Goals
Applicable translocations or reintroductions have authority endorsement and meet IUCN, CITES and IATA requirements
Animals are treated humanely; captive components meet ZAA standards
Project poses no unreasonable safety, financial or reputational risk
Organisation has no convictions for fraud, corruption, wildlife trade or animal cruelty
Project runs from January 2027 to December 2028

applicant_types.quote: Open to NGOs, community groups, and individuals, the field grants support both new and established conservation initiatives that would benefit from financial backing and specialist guidance.

geography.quote: Taronga's Field Conservation Grants provide vital funding and expert support to conservation projects making a real difference for wildlife, habitats and communities around the globe.

access.quote: Apply online with the option to download the Word version of the application to complete the questions before submitting online.

window.quote: Every two years, Taronga invests $200,000 in outstanding on-ground conservation programs, with individual grants of up to $20,000 awarded to the most impactful projects.

amount.quote: Every two years, Taronga invests $200,000 in outstanding on-ground conservation programs, with individual grants of up to $20,000 awarded to the most impactful projects.

effort.quote: Apply online with the option to download the Word version of the application to complete the questions before submitting online.
Applications reviewed by the Taronga Conservation Committee
additional checks conducted from July to August for shortlisted applicants

eligibility.quote: Projects must deliver clear, measurable benefits for species and/or habitats.
Projects must align with relevant SDGs.
Where applicable, projects must be endorsed by relevant authorities and comply with IUCN, CITES and IATA requirements (evidence required).
Humane treatment of animals is mandatory; captive components (if any) must meet ZAA (Zoo and Aquarium Association Australasia) standards.
Projects must not pose unreasonable safety, financial or reputational risk.
Organisations must have no convictions relating to fraud, corruption, wildlife trade or animal cruelty (declaration required).
Funding period: January 2027 - December 2028, with reporting at 12 months and project completion.
